chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, the children of Muslims are designated in the presence of God as intercessors and ones interceded for. So when they reach twelve years of age, good deeds are recorded for them. And when they reach puberty, evil deeds are recorded against them.

key_terms.السَّيِّئَاتُ: Evil deeds/sins — blameworthy acts recorded against one's account
key_terms.الْحَسَنَاتُ: Good deeds — meritorious acts recorded in one's account
key_terms.الْحُلُمَ: Puberty/maturity (hulm) — the Islamic legal age of full moral accountability
key_terms.شَافِعٌ وَمُشَفَّعٌ: Intercessor and one interceded for — dual role as both advocate and beneficiary of intercession
key_terms.مَوْسُومُونَ: Designated/marked ones — those given a special mark or status

ai.seo_question: At what age are children's good and bad deeds recorded in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the children of Muslims occupy a special status before God, serving as both intercessors and recipients of intercession. This hadith establishes a two-stage religious accountability for children: from age twelve, good deeds begin to be recorded in their favor, while the recording of sins only commences at puberty (bulugh). This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential understanding of the age of religious responsibility, where the transition to full moral-legal accountability (taklif) occurs at puberty, not at twelve.
